content.comment_body: I have an M-Flag in my diagram, which switches on the red backlight when an alert is triggered. The issue is that nothing else can turn on the backlight anymore; the screen remains dark except during an alert, at which point it goes red temporarily and then back to dark. How can I allow the backlight to be triggered by pressing a button as well?

In [product_name] [article_no], you can use M25 for continuous backlight. Place a marker in your workspace (in [product_name] Soft Comfort), right-click to view properties, and you'll see what each marker does.

This issue has been recognized by [company_name] for years but remains unresolved, and user suggestions seem to be overlooked. Whenever you use a backlighting flag in a [product_name] program, the white background lighting gets automatically disabled by pressing a button. You can configure the cursor keys (or function keys on the [product_name] operator device) for the white background flag, but you'll need to press ESC plus the cursor key each time.

I was struggling with having a continuously lit backlight, which I didn't want since it could wear out the LEDs over time. My solution was to set up ESC and arrow keys to temporarily activate the light.

analysis.insight_summary: Users face challenges with controlling backlight behavior on their [company_name] [product_name] device when using alert flags. Once the alert backlight is activated, other means like button presses no longer work to turn on the backlight, leaving the screen dark except during active alerts. Users are dissatisfied with the lack of flexible backlight options and believe [company_name] has not addressed these concerns despite longstanding feedback.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want the backlight to be activated both automatically during alerts and manually via button presses, while also avoiding continuous illumination to protect the device. They expect flexible and straightforward control over backlight options.
